featured_reviews.name: Smith Sirvel
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am extremely disappointed with my recent order from JP’s Lunch Home. I had ordered mutton gravy expecting a proper dish with meat, but what I received was just plain gravy with absolutely no mutton pieces in it.

This is not a minor mistake—the main component of the dish was completely missing. It feels misleading to charge customers for a mutton dish and deliver something that doesn’t even contain mutton.

What makes it worse is the inconvenience caused. I was left without a proper meal and had to go through the hassle of raising a complaint and following up for resolution. This is not the level of service one expects when ordering from a listed restaurant.

Restaurants need to take basic quality checks seriously before dispatching orders. Sending out incomplete items reflects very poorly on both the restaurant and the delivery platform.

I hope this feedback is taken seriously and necessary action is taken so that other customers do not face the same issue.

featured_reviews.name: Pratik P
featured_reviews.review_text:
**Absolutely disgraceful and humiliating experience**
This was not just bad service, this was outright insulting behavior by your staff.
A waiter named “Anna” displayed shocking levels of arrogance, rudeness and complete lack of basic etiquette. Our order was delayed by over 30 minutes and despite asking multiple times, we were blatantly ignored. When he finally chose to respond, it was with a careless and rude excuse about oil being refilled, as if customers are expected to tolerate such delays without communication.
What happened next was even worse.
When the food arrived my wife noticed that the halwa portion served was not even a spoonful, which is unacceptable. Another staff member showing basic common sense and courtesy, provided an extra serving as a goodwill gesture.
But then, in an act that was deeply disrespectful and outright shocking, this same waiter “Anna” walked up to our table and snatched the extra serving directly from our plate without even asking us, questioning why it was given.
This was extremely humiliating, especially in front of others. My wife felt insulted and we had to explicitly ask him to stay away from our table.
Let me be very clear, this is not a small mistake. This reflects complete failure in staff training, customer respect and management oversight.
We chose not to create a scene there, but this experience has ensured we will never return.
If this is the standard of service you tolerate, customers should think twice before visiting.
Train your staff or replace them because this level of behavior is unacceptable.
**Very very poor experience given by JP and your staff "Anna"**

Excellent Seafood restaurant in Mumbai. A very old mangalorian style seafood restaurant which also offers other non veg and veg dishes.

Food quality is exceptional. Very tasty food with least spices. Portions are quite sufficient.

Must try Butter Garlic Prawns and Butter Garlic Crab here. Also, Pomfret, Surmai, Bombil (Bombay Duck), crabs, lobsters are very very good and very tasty.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Pratap Lunch Home is a great spot if you’re craving prawns or fish. I tried their butter garlic prawns (4/5), tawa surmai fry (4/5), and Chettinad prawn biryani (4/5). It’s a chill place with a coastal vibe and homely food—highly recommend for a quick lunch.
Top Dishes
•	Butter garlic prawns: Fresh and flavorful, hitting all the right garlicky notes without overpowering the seafood.
•	Tawa surmai fry: Crispy edges with balanced spices, showcasing the fish’s natural freshness.
•	Chettinad prawn biryani: Spicy, aromatic, and generously portioned for a satisfying coastal twist.
Vibe and Service
The relaxed, sea-inspired ambience pairs perfectly with the comforting, home-style cooking. Quick service makes it ideal for lunch breaks in the Fort area.

featured_reviews.name: Niki Mitra
featured_reviews.review_text:
Discover the flavors of the sea at Pratap Lunch Home, a hidden restaurant de fruits de mer in the heart of Fort, Mumbai! This seafood and non-veg lover's paradise is a must-visit for any food enthusiast.

The LOVE:

- Delicious Food: The dishes are packed with flavor, and the portions are generous.
- Friendly Staff: The team is attentive and welcoming, making sure you feel at home.
- Cozy Ambiance: The AC section is a blessing, especially during peak hours.
- Alcohol Served: With a 10% VAT, you can pair your meal with a drink of your choice.

Must-Try Dishes:

- Mutton Bhuna: Tender, spicy, and utterly addictive. The quantity is impressive, and the quality shines through.
- Prawns Chilly Roast: Fresh, flavorful, and perfectly cooked. A must-try for seafood lovers.

We were impressed by the food, service, and ambiance. While peak hours can get busy, the wait is worth it. We're already planning our next visit to try more of their menu offerings.

If you're a seafood or non-veg lover, Pratap Lunch Home is a must-visit destination. With its rich flavors and cozy atmosphere, it's a great spot for a night out with friends or a special occasion.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a great culinary experience having lunch here on a weekday with my family. The place was not crowded at all, the ambience was calm and inviting with a home-like touch. We came with the intention of enjoying seafood and we achieved exactly that. I definitely recommend dining here and Pratap Lunch Home is now on my must-return list!

Food we ordered:
Bombil Fry - A Bombay staple and they did it justice. (5/5)
Lobster Chilly Roast - This was my favourite. Unbelievably good! I also liked how they were transparent in showing us the sizes and prices of the lobster they had in their catch and let us choose as per our preference. (5/5)
King Prawns Ghee Roast - Also really good. (5/5)
Shell Fish Sukka - Good masala but we were not blown away. We also had to be extra careful while eating as not all hard debris were cleaned from the shell fish. (3/5)
Squid Malabar - Crispy fried squid which I couldn't get enough of. (5/5)
Prawns Vijaywada - Decently flavoured prawns curry. (4/5)
Mutton Tawa Pulao - I've never had pulao done so well. Good sized portion too. (5/5)

We ordered the paan style surmai that was wrapped in a banana leaf and roasted, the sukha bhujane prawns and the crab soup. featured_reviews.name: Ralph Pinto
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dishes we had:
1. Crab Lollipop: 6/10
2. Thalis with Rice Bhakaris
-a. Surmai: 10/10
-b. Pomfret: 9/10
-c. Bombil: 7/10
3. Gulab Jamun: 3/10
4. Fresh Lime Soda: 8/10

Crab Lollipop wasn't great. I have had better elsewhere.
It lacked the basic crab taste and the coating too was very mild on flavor.

The thalis were awesome. The fish were very fresh and tasty that it made our day. Surmai was the best. It had the best flavor, followed by Pomfret and then the Bombil. Surmai and Pomfret were rawa fry with little masala. It was just plain batter fry for the Bombil. We make better Bombil fry at home, so yeah.
The rice bhakari tasted awesome when it was hot.
Dry Prawns/Jhinga/Javla tasted good with the bhakari.
The pomfret fish and curry was very fresh and tasty.
Solkadhi was chilled, felt refreshing and tasted good.

Gulab Jamun was the worst. Hard, dry and low on flavor.

Restaurant is smaller compared to the one near kemps corner. Cleanliness was decent. No washrooms. Only a basin is available. No Queue when we arrived at 8pm. But a queue started building later on.

Group of 4. Saturday Dinner. Mid April 2026.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Waited for 15 minutes to get a place.
They serve all sorts of packet Chaknas here like Moong Dal, Chakli, Seng, Chana, Roasted Chana Etc. These are all reasonably priced between 20 to 40.

We order Bombil Fry, Chicken Sukka, Kori Rotti and Neer Dosa & Solkadi
Being married to a Mangalorean and been a regular to Mangalorean outlets back in Kudla I know the taste very well. This was nowhere near sadly. The Bombil Fry being a Maharashtrian special was just oil fried with light red batter rather than Rawa Fry. Killed the appetite completely unfortunately. It was served a small bowl of Coconut gravy which was again very bland.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Hits and misses at this Mangalorean spot:

​I visited The Fisherman’s Kitchen on a Friday evening with high expectations, given the name and the positive reviews. While the atmosphere is family-friendly and the location is convenient (right below Bangur Nagar Metro with valet parking), the food was a mixed bag.
​The Standouts: The Pomfret in Banana Leaf was easily the highlight—the fish was incredibly fresh and perfectly cooked (4.5/5). Pairing the remaining gravy with Neer Dosa was the best part of the meal.
​The Letdowns: Unfortunately, the Prawns Tandoori didn't taste fresh (2.5/5), and the Crab Soup was watery with very little meat. The Kadipatta Chicken was also quite average; the chicken felt a bit tough and lacked that punchy Mangalorean flavor I was looking for.
​The Verdict:
​Ambience & Service: 3.5/5
​Alcohol Variety: 4/5
Food: 3/5
​Value for Money: 3/5
It’s a decent place for a family outing, and perhaps I caught them on an off-night, but for a seafood specialty restaurant, I expected more consistency in freshness.

⭐️⭐️⭐️ (6/10)
Tucked away in the greens of Aarey Colony, Hoy Maharaja Dhaba carries a rustic, countryside charm and gained quite a bit of attention through Instagram reels a few months ago.

The ambience leans into a traditional Maharashtrian dhaba vibe, with both outdoor and indoor (AC seating). We opted for the outdoor section, which was fairly comfortable thanks to well-placed fans that kept the space airy.

For food, we tried the pomfret fry and prawn fry. Both were fresh and decently spiced, making for a satisfactory meal. However, the flavours lacked the depth and authenticity you’d typically associate with coastal regions like Kashid or Dapoli.

The soul curry was enjoyable and comforting, while the lemon soda and kokam sharbat were refreshing additions to the meal. The detailing from the cutlery box to the plates, tumblers, and even the salt and pepper dispensers-did add a nice traditional touch to the overall setting.

That said, while the concept and ambience are appealing, the overall experience felt average and slightly overhyped. A decent visit, but not particularly memorable.

featured_reviews.name: Jyothis Thaliath
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited this place for lunch.  It’s a Marathi-style seafood speciality restaurant that promises authentic coastal flavours.

Ambience:
The outdoor dining area has a lovely rustic vibe, perfect for evenings or cooler days. However, during hot afternoons, it can get quite uncomfortable. There’s also an indoor, air-conditioned section, but the tables are tightly packed and the sofa type seating is bit aged and not very comfortable.

Food:
We tried two thalis — Mutton Thali and Surmai Thali.

The Mutton Thali was the highlight of our meal. The mutton chops were tender, perfectly spiced, and among the best I’ve had in a while. The gravy was rich and flavourful without being overpowering. The marrow-filled bone was a pleasant surprise.

The Surmai Thali, on the other hand, was average. The fish fry portion was large but just okay in taste.

I wouldn’t recommend the Thalis here overall as most of the side dishes were quite oily and didn’t match my palate (though Maharashtrians might enjoy that style).

Thalis are priced on the higher side (₹600–₹1200). While portions are generous enough to share, I’d suggest skipping the Thali and focusing on starters or individual seafood dishes for better value and taste.

We also tried Butter Garlic Prawns, which were disappointing. Also, the prawns added into Thali curries felt out of place. They could consider swapping a few prawn dishes for clams or calamari, which are common in  Malvani cuisine.

Overall:
Don't fall for the social media hype. It's good for a visit if you’re in Aarey and craving for seafood.

I usually write reviews when I truly like a place, but I felt the need to share this experience because my stomach was upset after eating here, which is concerning.

I visited this restaurant expecting authentic Ratnagiri/Konkan food, especially given the name and the 4-star rating. Unfortunately, the food did not meet those expectations at all.

I ordered a fish thali, but there was nothing about it that reflected true Konkan or Ratnagiri cuisine. The fish fry was bland, not properly marinated, and lacked basic flavor. I had to add salt, pepper, and lime myself just to make it edible. Authentic Konkan fish fry is known for its seasoning and marinade, which was completely missing here.

The fish curry was a simple onion-based gravy with no depth—no kokum, no tamarind, no spice, and not even the correct color of a traditional fish curry. The thali included bhakri, rice, fish fry, fish curry, sol curry, and a dry fish preparation. Except for the dry item, nothing tasted authentic or satisfying.

I also ordered chicken sukka, which is supposed to be dry and at least mildly spicy. What was served was more like a regular chicken curry with gravy, not dry at all, and completely lacking spice and flavor. It did not resemble chicken sukka in any way.

I had high expectations, but the food was nowhere near what one would expect from a place claiming to serve Ratnagiri or Konkan cuisine. This food does not represent Konkan food, not even remotely.

Overall, a very disappointing experience, and due to both the quality of the food and the health issue afterward, I would not recommend this restaurant.

featured_reviews.name: Kapil Jaiswal
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited Something’s Fishy last week to celebrate a family friend’s birthday.

If you’re a seafood lover, Something’s Fishy is the kind of place that instantly feels right. From the moment you step in, the ambience sets the mood. The interiors have a beautiful seafood-inspired theme, artistically done without being over the top. Subtle marine elements, thoughtful décor, and warm lighting make the space feel relaxed and inviting. It’s comfortable enough for a family dinner yet stylish enough for a special outing.

We tried quite a variety of dishes, and honestly, the experience from start to finish was satisfying.

Harra Channa ka Shorba (Chicken Soup): A comforting, mildly spiced chicken soup with fresh herb flavours. Light yet flavourful, it had a soothing warmth and well-balanced seasoning, perfect to begin the meal.

Chicken Gassi: Rich, coastal-style chicken curry with aromatic spices and creamy coconut base. The gravy was flavourful without being overpowering, and the chicken pieces were tender and well-cooked.

Appams: Soft, fluffy appams with delicate crisp edges. Light texture and subtle sweetness paired beautifully with the gassi gravies, soaking up flavours perfectly without becoming soggy.

Prawn Gassi: Fresh prawns cooked in traditional coastal gravy with coconut and spices. The prawns were juicy and tender, absorbing the rich masala while retaining their natural sweetness.

Butter Garlic Prawn: Perfectly sautéed prawns tossed in butter and garlic. Simple yet delicious, with a lovely aroma and balanced seasoning that allowed the freshness of the seafood to shine.

Surmai Fry: Crispy on the outside, moist and flaky inside. The fish was fresh, well-marinated, and fried just right, delivering bold coastal flavours without excessive oiliness.

Rawas Tandoori: Well-marinated rawas grilled to perfection in the tandoor. Smoky, juicy, and packed with spices, yet the fish remained soft and flavourful inside.

Squid Crispy Fried Rings: Lightly battered squid rings fried till crisp. Crunchy outside, tender inside, with balanced seasoning that made them addictive without feeling too heavy.

What stood out throughout the meal was the freshness of the seafood. Every dish felt thoughtfully prepared, not rushed. Portions were generous, and the flavours felt authentic rather than overly commercialised.

Service was smooth and friendly. The staff were attentive, happy to recommend dishes, and ensured everything was served at the right pace. They didn’t hover unnecessarily, which made the experience even more enjoyable.

Overall, Something’s Fishy delivers exactly what you expect from a seafood speciality restaurant — fresh ingredients, authentic coastal flavours, and a warm, pleasant ambience. It’s definitely a place I’d revisit whenever seafood cravings strike. Highly recommended for anyone who truly enjoys well-prepared seafood.

For instance, crab was quoted at around ₹5000 per kg (pre-processing), and a medium-sized pomfret fry, recommended by the staff—cost about ₹2000. The taste was decent, but not proportionate to the premium pricing.

The restaurant tends to be overcrowded in the evenings, likely due to limited seafood options in the surrounding area, drawing local seafood enthusiasts. However, compared to coastal cities like Visakhapatnam, Chennai, Bhubaneswar, Kolkata, or Kochi, the prices here are almost double without a corresponding difference in quality or experience.

Overall, it may appeal to those specifically seeking seafood in this locality, but in terms of value for money, it falls short.
N.B: After having Pomfret, I have been suffering from stomach upset (Food poisoning) and currently recovering.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Mahesh Lunch Home and had a very good experience overall.

The food was excellent, especially the seafood. The squid and prawns biryani were very tasty, well-cooked, and full of flavor. The mojito was refreshing and complemented the meal nicely.

The vibe of the place is great, making it a perfect spot for lunch with a comfortable and lively atmosphere.

Prices are a bit on the higher side, but the taste and quality make it worth it.

Overall, a great place to enjoy seafood and have a good dining experience.

featured_reviews.name: Daddyslittlelunchbox
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mahesh Lunch Lounge was an absolute standout and easily one of our best meals in India. We chose to eat here over the Taj after it was strongly recommended by locals — and we are so glad we listened. From start to finish, the experience was fantastic.

The food was exceptional, especially the seafood. The tiger prawns were MASSIVE — genuinely some of the biggest prawns we’ve ever seen, let alone eaten. They were cooked perfectly, full of flavour, and without doubt the best prawns we had in India. That’s saying something, especially as we truly believed Kerala couldn’t be beaten when it came to seafood.

Service was attentive and efficient without being overbearing, and the prices were surprisingly good for the quality and portion sizes. One bit of advice: order your starters before committing to mains — the portions are generous and we definitely over-ordered because everything sounded too good to miss (no regrets, just very full 😅).

Overall, Mahesh Lunch Lounge completely lived up to the hype and then some. Incredible food, huge portions, great service, and excellent value. If you’re debating where to eat — go here.

Follow ➡️ @daddylittlelunchbox

featured_reviews.name: Kanaka Shetty
featured_reviews.review_text:
Love the seafood here. They have some really authentic Mangalorean dishes. The prawns ghee roast, neer dosa, kori rotti & squid butter garlic are absolutely delicious.
Hospitality is top notch.

featured_reviews.name: Krishen Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
Excellent crab and delicious desert.

only complaint was that I would have preferred a pinch of salt but there was no salt shakers on the table!

Will visit again on my next trip to try out the items i could not this time around.

We had crab, chicken ghee roast, and a paneer dish, which was amongst the best we had  in India during our three week tour
